videos.script: Most of what CSS does is still. A box is where layout put it, a colour is a colour. {{still}} This lesson is about the three tools that make things move. {{transform}} A transform moves, turns or scales what is drawn, without moving anything else on the page. The book you point at lifts off the shelf, and its neighbours stay where they are. {{transition}} A transition takes a change that would happen instantly, a colour on hover, and spreads it over a fraction of a second, so the eye can follow it. {{animation}} An animation runs on its own, through steps you describe with keyframes: a notice that drops in, a spinner that turns. {{cheap}} Some properties are cheap to animate and some make the browser redo the whole layout sixty times a second. You will measure which. {{reader}} And not every reader wants movement. For some it causes real discomfort, and the operating system lets them say so. Every animation in this lesson listens. {{rule}} The rule underneath all of it: movement should explain something. If it only decorates, keep it short, or leave it out. {{close}}
